paragraphs.text: Forasmuch then as Christ suffered in the flesh, arm ye yourselves also with the same mind; for he that hath suffered in the flesh hath ceased from sin;
paragraphs.original: Χριστοῦ οὖν παθόντος σαρκὶ καὶ ὑμεῖς τὴν αὐτὴν ἔννοιαν ὁπλίσασθε, ὅτι ὁ παθὼν σαρκὶ πέπαυται ἁμαρτίας,
paragraphs.translit: Christou oun pathontos sarki kai hymeis tēn autēn ennoian hoplisasthe, hoti ho pathōn sarki pepautai hamartias,

paragraphs.text: that ye no longer should live the rest of your time in flesh to the lusts of men, but to the will of God.
paragraphs.original: εἰς τὸ μηκέτι ἀνθρώπων ἐπιθυμίαις ἀλλὰ θελήματι θεοῦ τὸν ἐπίλοιπον ἐν σαρκὶ βιῶσαι χρόνον.
paragraphs.translit: eis to mēketi anthrōpōn epithymiais alla thelēmati theou ton epiloipon en sarki biōsai chronon.

paragraphs.text: For the time past may suffice to have wrought the desire of the Gentiles, and to have walked in lasciviousness, lusts, winebibbings, revellings, carousings, and abominable idolatries:
paragraphs.original: ἀρκετὸς γὰρ ὁ παρεληλυθὼς χρόνος τὸ βούλημα τῶν ἐθνῶν κατειργάσθαι, πεπορευμένους ἐν ἀσελγείαις, ἐπιθυμίαις, οἰνοφλυγίαις, κώμοις, πότοις, καὶ ἀθεμίτοις εἰδωλολατρίαις.
paragraphs.translit: arketos gar ho parelēlythōs chronos to boulēma tōn ethnōn kateirgasthai, peporeumenous en aselgeiais, epithymiais, oinophlygiais, kōmois, potois, kai athemitois eidōlolatriais.

paragraphs.text: wherein they think strange that ye run not with [them] into the same excess of riot, speaking evil of [of]:
paragraphs.original: ἐν ᾧ ξενίζονται μὴ συντρεχόντων ὑμῶν εἰς τὴν αὐτὴν τῆς ἀσωτίας ἀνάχυσιν, βλασφημοῦντες·
paragraphs.translit: en hō xenizontai mē syntrechontōn hymōn eis tēn autēn tēs asōtias anachysin, blasphēmountes·

paragraphs.text: who shall give account to him that is ready to judge the living and the dead.
paragraphs.original: οἳ ἀποδώσουσιν λόγον τῷ ἑτοίμως ἔχοντι κρῖναι ζῶντας καὶ νεκρούς·
paragraphs.translit: hoi apodōsousin logon tō hetoimōs echonti krinai zōntas kai nekrous·

paragraphs.text: For unto this end was the gospel preached even to the dead, that they might be judged indeed according to men in the flesh, but live according to God in the spirit.
paragraphs.original: εἰς τοῦτο γὰρ καὶ νεκροῖς εὐηγγελίσθη ἵνα κριθῶσι μὲν κατὰ ἀνθρώπους σαρκὶ ζῶσι δὲ κατὰ θεὸν πνεύματι.
paragraphs.translit: eis touto gar kai nekrois euēngelisthē hina krithōsi men kata anthrōpous sarki zōsi de kata theon pneumati.

paragraphs.text: But the end of all things is at hand: be ye therefore of sound mind, and be sober unto prayer:
paragraphs.original: Πάντων δὲ τὸ τέλος ἤγγικεν. σωφρονήσατε οὖν καὶ νήψατε εἰς προσευχάς·
paragraphs.translit: Pantōn de to telos ēngiken. sōphronēsate oun kai nēpsate eis proseuchas·

paragraphs.text: above all things being fervent in your love among yourselves; for love covereth a multitude of sins:
paragraphs.original: πρὸ πάντων τὴν εἰς ἑαυτοὺς ἀγάπην ἐκτενῆ ἔχοντες, ὅτι ἀγάπη καλύπτει πλῆθος ἁμαρτιῶν·
paragraphs.translit: pro pantōn tēn eis heautous agapēn ektenē echontes, hoti agapē kalyptei plēthos hamartiōn·

paragraphs.text: using hospitality one to another without murmuring:
according as each hath received a gift, ministering it among yourselves, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God;
paragraphs.original: ἕκαστος καθὼς ἔλαβεν χάρισμα, εἰς ἑαυτοὺς αὐτὸ διακονοῦντες ὡς καλοὶ οἰκονόμοι ποικίλης χάριτος θεοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: hekastos kathōs elaben charisma, eis heautous auto diakonountes hōs kaloi oikonomoi poikilēs charitos theou·

paragraphs.text: if any man speaketh, [speaking] as it were oracles of God; is any man ministereth, [ministering] as of the strength which God supplieth: that in all things God may be glorified through Jesus Christ, whose is the glory and the dominion for ever and ever. Amen.
paragraphs.original: εἴ τις λαλεῖ, ὡς λόγια θεοῦ· εἴ τις διακονεῖ, ὡς ἐξ ἰσχύος ἧς χορηγεῖ ὁ θεός· ἵνα ἐν πᾶσιν δοξάζηται ὁ θεὸς διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ᾧ ἐστιν ἡ δόξα καὶ τὸ κράτος εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων· ἀμήν.
paragraphs.translit: ei tis lalei, hōs logia theou· ei tis diakonei, hōs ex ischyos hēs chorēgei ho theos· hina en pasin doxazētai ho theos dia Iēsou Christou, hō estin hē doxa kai to kratos eis tous aiōnas tōn aiōnōn· amēn.

paragraphs.text: Beloved, think it not strange concerning the fiery trial among you, which cometh upon you to prove you, as though a strange thing happened unto you:
paragraphs.original: Ἀγαπητοί, μὴ ξενίζεσθε τῇ ἐν ὑμῖν πυρώσει πρὸς πειρασμὸν ὑμῖν γινομένῃ ὡς ξένου ὑμῖν συμβαίνοντος,
paragraphs.translit: Agapētoi, mē xenizesthe tē en hymin pyrōsei pros peirasmon hymin ginomenē hōs xenou hymin symbainontos,

paragraphs.text: but insomuch as ye are partakers of Christ`s sufferings, rejoice; that at the revelation of his glory also ye may rejoice with exceeding joy.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλὰ καθὸ κοινωνεῖτε τοῖς τοῦ Χριστοῦ παθήμασιν χαίρετε, ἵνα καὶ ἐν τῇ ἀποκαλύψει τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ χαρῆτε ἀγαλλιώμενοι.
paragraphs.translit: alla katho koinōneite tois tou Christou pathēmasin chairete, hina kai en tē apokalypsei tēs doxēs autou charēte agalliōmenoi.

paragraphs.text: If ye are reproached for the name of Christ, blessed [are ye]; because the [Spirit] of glory and the Spirit of God resteth upon you.
paragraphs.original: εἰ ὀνειδίζεσθε ἐν ὀνόματι Χριστοῦ, μακάριοι, ὅτι τὸ τῆς δόξης καὶ τὸ τοῦ θεοῦ πνεῦμα ἐφʼ ὑμᾶς ἀναπαύεται.
paragraphs.translit: ei oneidizesthe en onomati Christou, makarioi, hoti to tēs doxēs kai to tou theou pneuma ephʼ hymas anapauetai.

paragraphs.text: For let none of you suffer as a murderer, or a thief, or an evil-doer, or as a meddler in other men`s matters:
paragraphs.original: μὴ γάρ τις ὑμῶν πασχέτω ὡς φονεὺς ἢ κλέπτης ἢ κακοποιὸς ἢ ὡς ἀλλοτριεπίσκοπος·
paragraphs.translit: mē gar tis hymōn paschetō hōs phoneus ē kleptēs ē kakopoios ē hōs allotriepiskopos·

paragraphs.text: but if [a man suffer] as a Christian, let him not be ashamed; but let him glorify God in this name.
paragraphs.original: εἰ δὲ ὡς Χριστιανός, μὴ αἰσχυνέσθω, δοξαζέτω δὲ τὸν θεὸν ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τούτῳ.
paragraphs.translit: ei de hōs Christianos, mē aischynesthō, doxazetō de ton theon en tō onomati toutō.

paragraphs.text: For the time [is come] for judgment to begin at the house of God: and if [it begin] first at us, what [shall be] the end of them that obey not the gospel of God?
paragraphs.original: ὅτι ὁ καιρὸς τοῦ ἄρξασθαι τὸ κρίμα ἀπὸ τοῦ οἴκου τοῦ θεοῦ· εἰ δὲ πρῶτον ἀφʼ ἡμῶν, τί τὸ τέλος τῶν ἀπειθούντων τῷ τοῦ θεοῦ εὐαγγελίῳ;
paragraphs.translit: hoti ho kairos tou arxasthai to krima apo tou oikou tou theou· ei de prōton aphʼ hēmōn, ti to telos tōn apeithountōn tō tou theou euangeliō;

paragraphs.text: And if the righteous is scarcely saved, where shall the ungodly and sinner appear?
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἰ ὁ δίκαιος μόλις σῴζεται, ὁ ἀσεβὴς καὶ ἁμαρτωλὸς ποῦ φανεῖται;
paragraphs.translit: kai ei ho dikaios molis sōzetai, ho asebēs kai hamartōlos pou phaneitai;

paragraphs.text: Wherefore let them also that suffer according to the will of God commit their souls in well-doing unto a faithful Creator.
paragraphs.original: ὥστε καὶ οἱ πάσχοντες κατὰ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ πιστῷ κτίστῃ παρατιθέσθωσαν τὰς ψυχὰς αὐτῶν ἐν ἀγαθοποιΐᾳ.
paragraphs.translit: hōste kai hoi paschontes kata to thelēma tou theou pistō ktistē paratithesthōsan tas psychas autōn en agathopoiia.
